claim: On Game of 24 with GPT-4, ToT (BFS, b=5) reaches 74% vs 4-9% for CoT and CoT-SC(100); b=1 already gives 45%. Re-open check: numbers confirmed in the paper text. Caveat: Others get lower or different values (see K02).
agent_test: Run our S6 tree vs CoT-SC on games 901-1000 at equal tokens with the same model.

claim: Independent re-runs of ToT on Game of 24 with GPT-4 disagree: 69% (AoT, b=5), 60.6% (b=3) and 34.3% (b=1) in XoT, 77% (b=3) and 65% (b=1) in Token Economies, vs original 74% (b=5) and 45% (b=1). Absolute ToT numbers depend on prompt and implementation.
agent_test: Do not quote 74% as our expectation; measure our own baseline on the same split.

claim: About 60% of CoT samples on Game of 24 already fail at the first step; the gain from search comes from pruning early.
agent_test: Log at which step wrong ideas die in our tree; test branching only at the first decision vs late.

claim: Backtracking and pruning each matter on crosswords: ToT 60% word success; no pruning 41.5%; no backtracking 20%. The evaluator wrongly prunes valid but rare words. Caveat: Only 20 games.
agent_test: Ablate backtrack and prune in our tree on a task with dead ends.

claim: The ToT gain needs a strong generator: GPT-3.5 ToT 19% vs 74% for GPT-4; GPT-4 generate + GPT-3.5 evaluate 64%; the reverse 31%. Token Economies agrees in direction (68% top-1 and 30% top-1 for the two mixes).
agent_test: Check the idea tree with a weaker model as evaluator at equal tokens.

claim: ToT is expensive: about 5.5k completion tokens per Game of 24 case (about 100 CoT trials), about 5x CoT on Creative Writing, 5-100x in general. Caveat: Cost figures come from one appendix table (re-opened and confirmed: IO $0.13, CoT $0.47, ToT $0.74).
agent_test: Always report accuracy at matched tokens; cap tree size.

claim: At matched budget with weak models, self-consistency can beat ToT; with GPT-4, ToT wins on Game of 24 (top-1 74% vs CoT-100 17%). Gain is large on a strong model, small or negative on a weak one. Caveat: Token Economies text says SC beats ToT for GPT-3.5, but its own table gives ToT top-1 25% vs SC 4%, and SC best-of-all 46% vs ToT 35%. Result depends on the metric.
agent_test: Compare tree vs sampling+vote at equal tokens for each model size we use.

claim: A random evaluator destroys ToT (GPT-4 top-1 0.0, best-of-all 0.04), so self-evaluation carries real signal on Game of 24; a GPT-3.5 evaluator gets 68% top-1 (72% best-of-all) at about one fifth of the cost. Caveat: Single task. Correction: evidence b14 listed 72% vs 76% as accuracy; these are best-of-all, top-1 is 68% vs 74%.
agent_test: Test our scorer against a random scorer and a cheaper scorer.

claim: On easy tasks where CoT already works ToT adds little: GSM8K 86->90, StrategyQA 82->83 (n=100, within noise); Xie et al. also find no gain on short commonsense chains. Caveat: n=100. Sys2Bench (d01) adds GPT-4o: GSM8K CoT 94.7 vs ToT 93.5, ProntoQA 91.8 vs 32.8.
agent_test: Only open the tree for items that fail a cheap first pass.

claim: LLM self-evaluation is unreliable where checking is hard: GPT-4 as verifier on Game of 24 has 87.0% accuracy but 10.4% false positives and 20.7% false negatives; self-critique lowered accuracy; a sound verifier raised it. Caveat: Tests generate-verify loops, not ToT BFS directly.
agent_test: Replace model scoring by code checks wherever a check exists; measure scorer false-positive rate.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without oracle feedback does not help and can hurt (CommonsenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1 after round 1, GPT-3.5). Caveat: Different loop than ToT but same weakness. The 75.8 -> 38.1 drop is partly a prompt effect.
agent_test: Never let the agent revise answers on its own judgment alone; require an external signal.

claim: When state and rules can be coded, having the LLM write the successor function and goal test and running plain BFS solved all 1362 Game of 24 instances (100%) in 1.92-6.83 s total; crosswords 20/20 with given candidate answers. Caveat: Needs exact formalisation; crossword used given candidates. Gap search: LLM+P and Silver show formal code beats per-node LLM planning only when a domain model exists and names are meaningful (d17, d18).
agent_test: Where possible let the agent write a small search program instead of calling the model per node.

claim: Putting a worked search trace in one prompt (AoT) matches ToT with 1-2 queries: 71% (1 query) vs ToT 69% (109 queries) on Game of 24; crossword words 52% vs 46.5%. Caveat: AoT authors ran ToT themselves.
agent_test: Compare a one-pass in-context search trace to the external tree at equal tokens.

claim: Merging thoughts (graph) beats trees on decomposable tasks: GoT sorting error 62% lower than ToT and over 31% cheaper (GPT-3.5, 128 numbers). Caveat: Tasks chosen to be mergeable.
agent_test: Allow merging of partial ideas only on decomposable items.

claim: Search with an LLM world model (RAP) helps planning: Blocksworld LLaMA-33B RAP(10) 100/86/26% at 2/4/6 steps vs GPT-4 CoT 50/63/40%; wins on short plans, loses at 6 steps with 10 iterations. Caveat: Small domain.
agent_test: Rewrite the problem state after each accepted step and judge only the remainder.

claim: Step-level self-evaluation beam search gives modest gains (GSM8K 85.5 vs 80.4, AQuA 64.2 vs 58.6, StrategyQA 77.2 vs 73.2 on Codex) and nothing on short commonsense chains. Caveat: Codex is deprecated.
agent_test: Use search only on long multi-step items.

claim: Tree search with a trained process reward model helps at low budget and medium-hard items but loses its edge at high budget and on easy items; MCTS was a poor compute trade vs a simpler reward-balanced tree search. Caveat: Needs a trained PRM; math only.
agent_test: Make tree width depend on budget and difficulty; test beam vs best-of-N across budgets.

claim: Multiple independent trees plus self-correction raise Game of 24 well above single ToT in the authors' own setups (FoT 96.84%, XoT 85.4%). Not independently replicated. Caveat: Method papers; some baseline rows copied from other papers; FoT uses about double the calls. Gap search: still no third-party run; FoT gain is partly self-correction and input enhancement (d20).
agent_test: Test two small trees vs one big tree at equal tokens.

claim: Best-first tree search over real environment states with a model value function raises GPT-4o web-agent success (VisualWebArena 18.9 -> 26.4%). Caveat: Needs a reversible environment.
agent_test: Not testable on a text-only agent.

claim: Training on search traces including dead ends beats training on optimal paths (Countdown 51.3% vs 25.7%); Searchformer solves 93.7% of Sokoban. Training results, not prompting. Caveat: Training.
agent_test: Out of scope for a scaffold-only agent.

claim: Reasoning models do search-like backtracking inside one chain; DeepSeek-R1 team dropped MCTS as impractical; o1-preview 97.8% on Blocksworld vs 62.6% for the best LLM, but 23.6% on 20-40 step plans. Caveat: R1 negative result is prose only. Gap search: plain o1 beats ToT-on-GPT-4o (d02); outer search on o3-mini lifts HLE sample 13 to 37 with Best-of-N (d03, n=100); no clean ToT-on-reasoning-model test found.
agent_test: If the base model is a reasoning model, test whether an external tree adds anything over its own chain.

claim: Prompted CoT gains in planning are example-bound and decay with problem size; structured search prompts may share this limit (inference, not tested for ToT). Caveat: Covers CoT, not ToT.
agent_test: Test the tree on instances larger than the prompt examples.

claim: Creative Writing: ToT 7.56 vs CoT 6.93 vs IO 6.19 by a GPT-4 judge; humans preferred ToT 41 vs 21 (38 similar) in 100 pairs. Judge is the same model family; raters were authors. Caveat: Self-judged. Gap search: independent work finds LLM judges of creative writing do not track experts (d16).
agent_test: Judge open-task gains with an independent blinded judge.

claim: The tree gain over equal-budget sampling on current models depends on task type. On GPT-4o, ToT beats SC@5 on Game of 24 (62 vs 18) but loses on GSM8K, ProntoQA, HotPotQA and Blocksworld. SC@5 is not token-matched.
agent_test: Route to a tree only for checkable, multi-step puzzle-like tasks; use samples plus vote elsewhere.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Prompt-only search beats equal-candidate sampling on 2024-25 models when a hard evaluator exists: Mind Evolution 95.6 vs Best-of-N 55.6 on TravelPlanner at 800 candidates; PlanSearch 77.0 vs 55.6 pass@200. No such result with an LLM-only evaluator was found.
agent_test: Bind every tree to a checker (code, unit test, constraint check) when one exists.

claim: A reasoning model without a tree beats a non-reasoning model with a tree (o1 Blocksworld 99.2 vs GPT-4o ToT 12.4). Gains from wrapping reasoning models are small on code (o1-mini PlanSearch +0.5) and QwQ (FoT +0.6 MATH500), larger on HLE with Best-of-N (13 to 37, n=100). Long chains also hurt: shortest chains are more accurate.
agent_test: On a reasoning model use parallel samples with a short-chain preference before any tree.

claim: Without a checker, the pick step is the bottleneck: majority vote and reward model gain 0.9 points while coverage rises 15; an LLM judge of research ideas agrees with humans 53.3% (chance 50%); LLM judges of creative writing do not correlate with experts.
agent_test: For uncheckable idea tasks do not trust a model score alone; dedup, use pairwise blind ranking, and keep human or external ranking.

claim: Models favour their own output; a panel of three diverse small models beat one GPT-4 judge (kappa NQ 0.763 vs 0.627) at 7-8x lower cost. Not tested inside a tree.
agent_test: Score thoughts with a different model or prompt than the generator, blind and order-randomised.

claim: Width rule without a trained reward model: sample until answers agree (3.2x fewer samples, -0.07% accuracy); easy items revise sequentially, medium-hard branch (Snell, needs PRM or pass-rate for difficulty). A prompt-only difficulty-routed width rule is not tested.
agent_test: Use agreement among 3-5 samples as difficulty signal: unanimous means stop, split means widen.

claim: Formal code for successor and goal test beats per-node LLM calls only where a domain model exists (LLM+P Blocksworld 90 vs ToT 0; Silver GPT-4 0.90 on 3 of 7 domains, 0.01-0.10 on two). Unformalisable tasks cannot use this route.
agent_test: Try to write a checker or simulator first; fall back to the LLM tree only if none can be coded.
